name: Oral submucous fibrosis
specialty: Oral medicine / Oral and maxillofacial surgery

reference.source: Oral medicine and oral pathology reference texts
clinicalPearls: A chronic progressive fibrosing disease of the oral mucosa strongly linked to areca (betel) nut chewing
Patients develop burning on eating spicy food, blanching and stiffening of the mucosa and progressive limitation of mouth opening
Palpable fibrous bands in the buccal mucosa and a rigid, pale mucosa are characteristic
It is a recognised oral potentially malignant disorder with a significant risk of squamous cell carcinoma
It is most prevalent in South and South-East Asian populations and their diaspora
Management includes strict habit cessation, medical measures to improve mouth opening and surgery for severe trismus, with lifelong cancer surveillance
reference.pathophysiology: Oral submucous fibrosis is driven chiefly by arecoline and other alkaloids in areca nut, which stimulate fibroblast proliferation and collagen synthesis while reducing collagen breakdown, leading to excessive deposition of dense fibrous tissue in the lamina propria and submucosa. Chronic inflammation and juxta-epithelial hyalinisation cause progressive mucosal stiffening and trismus, and epithelial atrophy with altered turnover increases susceptibility to malignant transformation. The result is an irreversible fibrotic and potentially premalignant state.
additionalInvestigations: Clinical assessment of mouth opening and fibrous bands
Biopsy to confirm fibrosis and exclude dysplasia or carcinoma
Detailed habit history of areca nut and tobacco use
Assessment of nutritional status and anaemia where relevant
redFlags: Development of a non-healing ulcer, red patch or mass suggesting carcinoma
Weight loss or difficulty maintaining nutrition
reference.prognosis: The fibrosis is largely irreversible and progressive if the habit continues; cessation and treatment can improve symptoms, but the elevated lifelong risk of oral cancer necessitates ongoing surveillance.
pitfalls: Failing to counsel firmly on areca nut and tobacco cessation
Confusing early disease with lichen planus or leukoplakia
Underestimating the functional impact of progressive trismus
